context:
Meet Aldehydes and Ketones: Their Structures / Structures from NCERT page 230.
Every one has a carbonyl group, C=O (in pink).
Aldehydes: C=O at the end of the chain, as -CHO (3-Oxopentanal, 4-Nitrobenzaldehyde).
Ketones: C=O inside the chain (2,4-Dimethylpentan-3-one).
alt: Structures from the NCERT book (page 230): 3-Oxopentanal, 2,4-Dimethylpentan-3-one, 4-Nitrobenzaldehyde and Propane-1,2,3-tricarbaldehyde, with each carbonyl group (C=O, and CHO in aldehydes) shown in pink.
description: Four structural formulas show aldehydes and ketones, with each carbonyl group (C=O) highlighted in pink. Students should notice that an aldehyde's C=O sits at the end of a carbon chain as -CHO, while a ketone's C=O sits inside the chain, flanked by carbon on both sides.
